Fig. 2: Human–Robot Hardware Co-design. (a,b) Human demonstration and robot deployment interfaces.
(c,d) Corresponding fingertip
tactile-sensor placements and wrist-camera configurations reduce mismatch across embodiments.

Fig. 3: Tac-Retarget .
(a) Fingertip pose alignment tracks the demonstrated
fingertip positions and orientations in the camera frame.
(b) Contact alignment matches the patch center and active
taxels between the human and robot fingertips.
(c) A tactile-activated contact graph preserves the
demonstrated spatial relations among active contacts
within and across the two hands.
Weighting terms and regularization are omitted for clarity.
Fig. 4: Human-to-robot data generation. From left to right: raw human demonstrations, removal masks, inpainted scenes, and synthesized robot-domain observations.
Fig. 5: Four contact-rich tasks evaluated in our experiments.

Fig. 6: (a) Action replay success rates across four tasks,
with 20 converted human demonstrations replayed per task
under matched initial scene conditions.
(b) Real-robot success rates of GR00T N1.7 [ 21 ] policies
fine-tuned on 60 demonstrations per task from each data source.
(c) Average collection time per successful demonstration,
including failed attempts and scene resets.
Multipliers indicate collection speedups. Error bars show standard deviation over the four tasks.

Fig. 7: Observation comparison across data domains.
(a) Multi-view observations from real-robot and human-derived data.
(b) VLM feature distributions before the action expert.

Fig. 8: Qualitative comparison of Tac-Retarget, its
kinematic-only variant, and retargeting baselines.

Fig. 9: Real-robot policy success rates comparing Tac-Retarget,
its tactile ablations and existing retargeting methods. Error bars show standard deviation over the four tasks.

Fig. 10: Real-robot policy success rates under different
policy and pretraining settings. Error bars show standard deviation over the four tasks.

Fig. 11: Reconstruction of camera-frame tactile
fingertip poses. (a) Wrist-mounted AprilTag fiducial frames detected in the
egocentric image.
(b) Manus fingertip positions (red) reconstructed using the
calibrated wrist-to-cube transforms.
(c) Tactile-sensor origins (blue) obtained by applying the
fixed sensor-to-fingertip mounting transform.
(d) Close-up of the fixed spatial offsets between the Manus
fingertips (red) and tactile-sensor origins (blue).
